column3: The Hebrew says that he built the house for the LORD; BSB says that he began to build it.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeatedly calls the building “the house”; BSB uses “the temple.”
The Hebrew says that he made the windows; BSB expresses the making through “had.” It calls the building “house,” where BSB uses “temple.”
The Hebrew leaves the builder unnamed and repeats “around”; BSB names Solomon and rearranges the surrounding structure and side rooms.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names “the axe”; BSB uses “chisel.” It calls the building “house,” where BSB uses “temple.”
The Hebrew calls the chamber “middle” and its side “right”; BSB says “bottom floor” and “south side.”
The Hebrew leaves the builder unnamed and says “house”; BSB supplies Solomon and uses “temple.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “this house,” “My word,” and “with you”; BSB uses “this temple,” “the promise,” and “through you.”
The Hebrew says “sons of Israel”; BSB uses “Israelites.”
The Hebrew says “house”; BSB uses “temple.”
The Hebrew repeats “the house” in describing its walls and floor; BSB condenses those repetitions and calls it “the temple.”
The Hebrew says “from the floor to the walls”; BSB uses “from floor to ceiling.”
The Hebrew says “the house, that is, the hall in front”; BSB supplies the reference “this room.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the preparer unnamed and calls the building “house”; BSB names Solomon and uses “temple.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew states the final overlaying with an active verb; BSB turns it into a passive relative clause.
The Hebrew says “the whole house” twice; BSB interprets this as the whole interior and completion of everything.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew measures from the ends of the wings to the ends of the wings; BSB condenses this to “the full wingspan.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew separately gives the first cherub’s height and says that the second was likewise; BSB combines them as “each cherub.”
The Hebrew says that they spread the wings of the cherubim; BSB expresses the spread wings as a passive circumstance.
